# Binaries that fail to launch on iOS because a symbol is missing.
#
#     ./machomorph.py --scan ... --exclude-from data/blocklist_symbols.txt
#
# GENERATED by tools/blocklist_from_probe.py from measurements/device_probe_2026-08-31_noblocklist.tsv.
# Do not edit by hand -- re-probe and regenerate. The list it replaced was
# hand-maintained and drifted from its own measurements; see
# measurements/retired_blocklist_ios.txt.
#
# Every line names the symbol that blocked it, as an inline comment,
# because a missing symbol is a SNAPSHOT and not a verdict: it can be
# fixed by a rename, a forwarding shim, or a newer iOS. To retire a
# symbol, delete the lines naming it and re-probe:
#
#     grep -v '_the$SYMBOL' data/blocklist_symbols.txt > new
#
# These binaries are inert rather than dangerous -- dyld kills them at
# launch, so shipping one costs disk space and a confusing error, not
# correctness. Excluding them is a tidiness decision, and the evidence to
# reverse it is on the line.

# 285 binaries, 149 distinct symbols.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HELD BACK -- deliberately NOT excluded. The missing symbol is imported by a
# library THIS CRYPTEX BUNDLES, so the failure is ours to fix rather than a
# limit of iOS. Excluding these would hide our own bug and drop working tools.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   _syslog$DARWIN_EXTSN                                  FIXED 2026-08-31
#     imported by bundled libcrypto.46.dylib
#     blocked: checkgid, openssl, tcpdump
#     dsc_lift.sh now renames it to plain _syslog after the rebind, so the
#     library loads. Awaiting a device probe to confirm.
#   _ASN1_STRING_get0_data                                FIXED 2026-08-31
#     imported by bundled libcurl.4.dylib
#     blocked: curl
#     Never a separate bug: it is a weak import from libcrypto, and the
#     "Expected in: <no uuid> unknown" was dyld reporting that libcrypto had
#     failed to load for the reason above. One root cause, three tools.
